To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a model transformation from UML protocol state machines, optionally complemented by object constraint language specifications, to the Alloy language, which enables automatic validation and verification of the UML models.

(i) PSMs can be automatically translated to Alloy; (ii) the resulting Alloy models can be automatically validated and verified; and (iii) the Alloy models can be easily integrated in current software development processes.

(1) the proposed model transformation enables automatic verification and integration of PSMs and Alloy; (2) the model transformation is based on the Alloy Analyzer; (3) it is implemented as a Java application; (4) it is available at https://sites.google.com/site/paulomartinsneto/AlloyPSM
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) the specification and validation of PMSs in Alloy, (b) the integration of Alloy in the software development life cycle, (c) the integration of PSMs and OCL in Alloy, (d) the integration of the model transformation with a CASE tool, namely MagicDraw.
the application of Alloy for the analysis of UML Protocol State Diagrams.
the development of a methodology and tool to support the specification, analysis and verification of UML PSMs in Alloy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Alloy can be applied to validate and verify UML PSMs, complemented with OCl, and that the proposed approach is a good candidate for integration into current software development processes.

the model transformation from PMSs, optionally complement with OCL specifications to Alloy, is an effective way to support the verification and validation of the external behavior in the development of software systems.
Alloy is a good candidate for the validation and verification of PSMs.

PSMs can now be specified and analyzed with Alloy.

PSMs are now first-class citizens in the Alloy world, with the possibility of using them for requirements analysis and testing, and also as a way to specify the external behavior of classes, components or interfaces in Alloy models.
PSMs, complemented with OML, are now first-class citizens of the Alloy community.

Alloy, which has been used for modeling and verification of software systems, can also be used for modeling and validation of PMSs.
